extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and producing common types of local news items (municipal work, safety campaigns, business mergers, real-estate notices, market reports, etc.) with the factual detail and presentation each requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: MUNICIPAL WORK
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-operation between the city and the public service corporations to a greater extent than before in order to prevent the tearing up of newly laid pavement is expected to result from the Dickinson-street case...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report municipal work with concrete local details: name streets and locations (e.g., Dickinson-street), identify responsible officials (e.g., Samuel L. Wheeler, Fred H. Clark), explain legal or procedural obligations (e.g., orders to put wires underground, annual mile requirement), describe timelines and sequencing (e.g., track work to precede paving), mention cooperation or conflict between city and companies, include quotes or official statements, and cover practical impacts on residents and infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEW MUNICIPAL EQUIPMENT
rubrics_metrics.description: Bursting water mains are not so great a menace in Boston since the water department installed a motor truck with a power appliance for quickly closing the heavy gates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When covering municipal equipment, describe the problem being solved, explain how the new device works (mechanism, components — e.g., universal wrench socket, worm gear, aluminum housing), give performance improvements (e.g., reduces 45 minutes of four men’s work to ten minutes by one man), include inventor/official names and manufacturer details, operational requirements (response to alarms, crew duties), safety features (indicators, counters, shear pins), and concrete examples of scale/impact (quantities of water, gate sizes).

rubrics_metrics.name: SAFETY CAMPAIGN
rubrics_metrics.description: With the belief that Long Island will be the touring ground for more motor cars this summer ... James A. McCrea ... has announced the beginning of a campaign of sign display asking the public to co-operate with the railroad in saving human life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety-campaign pieces should communicate the campaign’s purpose, describe visible interventions (size/design of signs, lighting), give direct sample messaging (e.g., 'THIS SIGN MAY SAVE YOUR LIFE TODAY.' and 'When approaching a crossing please stop, look and listen.'), report scale and cost (number of crossings, number of signs, expense of guarding), include official endorsement and calls to action, contrast local practice with alternatives (e.g., gate color in Europe), and note accompanying publicity (bulletins, repeated pleas) and any operational details about where and why measures are being taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: BUSINESS MERGER
rubrics_metrics.description: Through a deal involving about $400,000, the Milwaukee-Western Fuel company has bought out entirely the docks, property and business of the Northwestern Fuel company's Milwaukee branch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover mergers with transactional specifics: purchase price, assets acquired (docks, inventory tonnage), physical details (dock dimensions, river locations, capacity in tons), business consequences (branch closure/continuation, employees retained), company histories and sales volumes, expected business impact (increase in tonnage), officers/names of principals, terms (assumption of contracts), and contextual comments (whether consolidation or acquisition). Use direct figures and locations to convey scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEW FEATURE IN MANUFACTURING
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the story of a world war, a despairing manufacturer, and a cow's ear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature stories about manufacturing should frame the human problem (supply disruption due to war), trace the solution-seeking process (manufacturer seeks help, civic agency investigates), explain the technical substitution found (cow's ear hair as brush material), quote experts and describe local industry adaptation (stockyards, brokers, brush makers), and report outcomes (plant running, orders restored). Use narrative elements to show cause, inventive workaround, local resourcefulness, and economic impact on workers and production.

rubrics_metrics.name: REAL ESTATE (property sale / conversion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Another of the old exclusive homes ... is to be given over to business uses, the Arthur Meeker residence at 1815, which has been purchased by D. C. Heath & Co., school book publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Real-estate reports should include buyer and seller names, sale price, precise addresses, physical description (stories, room counts, lot dimensions, garages), intended new use (offices, stores, hotels), occupancy or move-in dates, negotiators/agents, historical notes (when built, past owners, remodels), and how the property will be adapted (e.g., garage enlargement for stock room). Give concrete measurements and dates to show significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: REAL ESTATE (land development / subdivision)
rubrics_metrics.description: The six and a half acre plot of ground at 5th and Cayuga streets ... has been sold ... to a builder, who will begin the work of developing the ground in the spring by the erection of about 30 houses on the 5th street front and 65 houses on Reese street.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For land-development pieces include acreage and exact boundaries/frontages, sale price, intended development plans (number and location of houses), reserved parcels and intended uses (e.g., hotel site retained by seller), historical/current use of the property (picnic park), and significance to the neighborhood (largest transaction in years). Provide dimensions and projected uses to indicate scale and community impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSED NEW HOTEL
rubrics_metrics.description: Another large hotel, to cost about $1,250,000, is to be erected ... at the corner of Washington and Avery streets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting on proposed major buildings, include project cost, site location, contracting parties (owners, contractors, architects, consulting architects), leasing arrangements (tenant/lessee and term), distribution of space (stores vs. guest rooms, public rooms placement), structural and finish details (fireproofing, materials, floor types, heating/ventilation), special amenities (rathskeller, sample rooms), and design/architectural style. Note construction standards, approximate timelines, and long-term commercial intentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: MUNICIPAL BOND SALE
rubrics_metrics.description: City Treasurer E. T. Tifft yesterday surprised himself and financial experts as well by selling a bond issue of $1,000,000 at remarkably good terms ... the issue was sold to N. W. Harris & Co ... bringing the interest rate down to 4.30 per cent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial/municipal bond reporting should state issue size, purchaser(s), bid prices and premiums, resulting effective interest rates, breakdown of loan purposes and maturities (itemized loans, years, and coupons), compare with past issues and market context, name bidding institutions and rankings, and include commentary on market implications (confidence revival, tax-exempt status, federal tax treatment). Provide exact figures and interpretive analysis from financial bureaus or experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: RAILROAD DIVIDEND
rubrics_metrics.description: Directors of the Pennsylvania company declared yesterday a semi-annual dividend of 1 per cent as against the usual dividend of 4 per cent at this time of the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corporate dividend stories should state declared dividend amounts and compare to historical norms, give company capital figures and the monetary effect of cuts (total dollars and per-share impact), explain corporate structure/ownership relations affecting distributions, provide recent earnings percentages, note regulatory or market actions affecting revenue (e.g., ICC rate decisions), and include directors’ explanations for changes (traffic/revenue decreases). Use precise percentages and historical comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: RETAIL PRICE OF BEEF (market reassurance piece)
rubrics_metrics.description: That there is no truth in the report ... that the record-breaking drought in Kansas will cause the retail prices of beef to go to unheard of prices in the winter, is the declaration of local provision dealers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For price-reassurance/commodity stories gather statements from local dealers/packing houses, present opposing claims and rebuttals, explain geographic scope of supply disruptions (confined sections vs. national effect), cite current price evidence and historical comparisons for specific cuts, discuss wholesale vs. retail margins and costs, and address public concerns about profiteering. Use expert quotes to contextualize price expectations regionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOCAL MARKET PRICES (produce market report)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peaches, peaches, and then more peaches, meet the eye of the visitor to the market section ... Wholesale prices are reasonable ... but prices at retail rarely fall below a certain level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Market-report items should describe available produce and variety (origins, e.g., Georgia, Connecticut, New Jersey), note wholesale vs. retail price behavior, explain factors affecting prices (freights, packing costs, shipment varieties), recommend buyer tips (inspect freestone vs. clingstone, avoid half-rotten fruit), provide concrete price ranges (per dozen, small baskets, wholesale/retail), and include packing/box cost details. Include sensory description and practical buying advice for readers.
